arxiv-2105-03131.title: Code2Image: Intelligent Code Analysis by Computer Vision Techniques and Application to Vulnerability Prediction
arxiv-2105-03131.creator: Zeki Bilgin
arxiv-2105-03131.description: Abstract Intelligent code analysis has received increasing attention in parallel with the remarkable advances in the field of machine learning (ML) in recent years. A major challenge in leveraging ML for this purpose is to represent source code in a useful form that ML algorithms can accept as input.

arxiv-2205-04887.title: Search-Based Testing of Reinforcement Learning To appear in Proceedings of IJCAI-ECAI 2022, ( ijcai.org ).
arxiv-2205-04887.creator: Martin Tappler, Filip Cano Córdoba, Bernhard K. Aichernig, Bettina Könighofer
arxiv-2205-04887.description: Abstract Evaluation of deep reinforcement learning (RL) is inherently challenging. Especially the opaqueness of learned policies and the stochastic nature of both agents and environments make testing the behavior of deep RL agents difficult. We present a search-based testing framework that enables a wide range of novel analysis capabilities for evaluating the safety and performance of deep RL agents.

arxiv-2212-10860.creator: in a turbulent Navier-Stokes fluid

arxiv-2302-00391.title: PresSim: An End-to-end Framework for Dynamic Ground Pressure Profile Generation from Monocular Videos Using Physics-based 3D Simulation
arxiv-2302-00391.creator: Lala Shakti Swarup Ray 1 2 , Bo Zhou 1 2 , Sungho Suh 1 2 and Paul Lukowicz 1 2
arxiv-2302-00391.description: Abstract Ground pressure exerted by the human body is a valuable source of information for human activity recognition (HAR) in unobtrusive pervasive sensing. While data collection from pressure sensors to develop HAR solutions requires significant resources and effort, we present a novel end-to-end framework, PresSim, to synthesize sensor data from videos of human activities to reduce such effort significantly.

arxiv-2310-03272.title: T-GAE: Transferable Graph Autoencoder for Network Alignment
arxiv-2310-03272.creator: Jiashu He, Charilaos Kanatsoulis, Alejandro Ribeiro
arxiv-2310-03272.description: Abstract Network alignment is the task of establishing one-to-one correspondences between the nodes of different graphs. Although finding a plethora of applications in high-impact domains, this task is known to be NP-hard in its general form. Existing optimization algorithms do not scale up as the size of the graphs increases.

arxiv-2311-00799.title: Latent space representations of cosmological fields
arxiv-2311-00799.creator: Sambatra Andrianomena, Sultan Hassan
arxiv-2311-00799.description: Abstract We investigate the possibility of learning the representations of cosmological multifield dataset from the CAMELS project. We train a very deep variational encoder on images which comprise three channels, namely gas density (Mgas), neutral hydrogen density (HI), and magnetic field amplitudes (B). Using a subsample of 47 galaxies ( 0.27 < z < 0.36 0.27<z<0.

arxiv-2401-13728.title: Astrophysical Axion Bounds: The 2024 Edition
arxiv-2401-13728.description: Abstract We review the current status of astrophysical bounds on QCD axions, primarily based on the observational effects of nonstandard energy losses on stars, including black-hole superradiance. Over the past few years, many of the traditional arguments have been reexamined both theoretically and using modern data and new ideas have been put forth.

arxiv-2502-10864.title: Recursions for quadratic rotation symmetric functions weights
arxiv-2502-10864.creator: Thomas W. Cusick
arxiv-2502-10864.description: Abstract A Boolean function in n n variables is rotation symmetric (RS) if it is invariant under powers of ρ ⁡ ( x 1 , … , x n ) = ( x 2 , … , x n , x 1 ) \rho(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})=(x_{2},\ldots,x_{n},x_{1}) .

arxiv-2503-00622.title: Computation of the semiclassical outflux emerging from a collapsing spherical null shell
arxiv-2503-00622.creator: Amos Ori, Noa Zilberman
arxiv-2503-00622.description: Abstract We consider a minimally coupled, massless quantum scalar field Φ ^ \hat{\Phi} propagating in the background geometry of a four-dimensional black hole formed by the collapse of a spherical thin null shell, with a Minkowski interior and a Schwarzschild exterior.

arxiv-2504-15292.title: Range Counting Oracles for Geometric Problems
arxiv-2504-15292.creator: Anne Driemel, Morteza Monemizadeh, Eunjin Oh, Frank Staals, David P. Woodruff
arxiv-2504-15292.description: Abstract In this paper, we study estimators for geometric optimization problems in the sublinear geometric model. In this model, we have oracle access to a point set with size n n in a discrete space [ Δ ] d [\Delta]^{d} , where queries can be made to an oracle that responds to orthogonal range counting requests.

arxiv-2506-12035.title: MARché: Fast Masked Autoregressive Image Generation with Cache-Aware Attention
arxiv-2506-12035.creator: Chaoyi Jiang, Sungwoo Kim, Lei Gao, Hossein Entezari Zarch, Won Woo Ro, Murali Annavarm, [1em] University of Southern California, Yonsei University {chaoyij, leig, entezari, annavara}@usc.edu{sungwoo.kim, wro}@yonsei.ac.kr
arxiv-2506-12035.description: Abstract Masked autoregressive (MAR) models unify the strengths of masked and autoregressive generation by predicting tokens in a fixed order using bidirectional attention for image generation. While effective, MAR models suffer from significant computational overhead, as they recompute attention and feed-forward representations for all tokens at every decoding step, despite most tokens remaining semantically stable across steps.

arxiv-2506-23134.title: Markov Chains of Evolutionary Games with a Small Number of Players
arxiv-2506-23134.creator: Ath. Kehagias
arxiv-2506-23134.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ath. Kehagias. We construct and study the transition probability matrix of evolutionary games in which the number of players is finite (and relatively small) of such games. We use a simplified version of the population games studied by Sandholm. After laying out a general framework we concentrate on specific examples, involving the Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, the Iterated Stag Hunt, and the Rock-Paper-Scissors game. Also we consider several revision protocols: Best Response, Pairwise Comparison, Pairwise Proportional Comparison etc.

arxiv-2509-02819.title: Protecting Legacy Wireless Systems Against Interference: Precoding and Codebook Approaches Using Massive MIMO and Region Constraints A preliminary version of this paper was presented at the 2024 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers. This work is in part supported by the National Sc
arxiv-2509-02819.creator: Sameer Mathad, Taejoon Kim, and David J. Love
arxiv-2509-02819.description: Abstract The ever-increasing demand for high-speed wireless communication has generated significant interest in utilizing frequency bands that are adjacent to those occupied by legacy wireless systems. Since the legacy wireless systems were designed based on often decades-old assumptions about wireless interference, utilizing these new bands will result in interference with the existing legacy users.

arxiv-2511-06382.title: Analysis of elastic α \alpha - 12 C scattering with machine learning in the cluster effective field theory
arxiv-2511-06382.creator: Myeong-Hwan Mun, Jubin Park, Chang Ho Hyun, Shung-Ichi Ando
arxiv-2511-06382.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Myeong-Hwan Mun, Jubin Park, Chang Ho Hyun, Shung-Ichi Ando. We analyze the elastic α \alpha - 12 C scattering including the contribution of resonance states below the p p - 15 N breakup threshold energy. We use the cluster effective field theory in which scattering amplitude is expanded in terms of the effective range expansion parameters for the angular momentum states from l = 0 l=0 to l = 6 l=6 .

pmc-10650641.title: Rethinking IL-1 Antagonism in Respiratory Viral Infections: A Role for IL-1 Signaling in the Development of Antiviral T Cell Immunity
pmc-10650641.creator: Bram Van Den Eeckhout, Marlies Ballegeer, Jozefien De Clercq, Elianne Burg, Xavier Saelens, Linos Vandekerckhove, Sarah Gerlo, Daniela Novick, Waipo Chong
pmc-10650641.description: IL-1R integrates signals from IL-1α and IL-1β, and it is widely expressed across tissues and immune cell types. While the expression pattern and function of IL-1R within the innate immune system is well studied, its role in adaptive immunity, particularly within the CD8 T cell compartment, remains underexplored.

pmc-11454826.title: 7598 A Humanized PTH Receptor Mouse Model Of Eiken Syndrome: Delayed Bone Mineralization Caused By A Receptor C-tail Truncation
pmc-11454826.creator: Jakob Höppner, Patrick Hanna, Marc Nathan Wein, Harald Jueppner, Thomas James Gardella, Roberto Civitelli, Ignacio A Portales-Castillo

Abstract The parathyroid hormone receptor-1 (PTH1R) plays a key role in bone development and acts in the growth plates in response to PTHrP ligand.

pmc-11602816.title: Multi-Grid Reaction-Diffusion Master Equation: Applications to Morphogen Gradient Modelling
pmc-11602816.creator: Radek Erban, Stefanie Winkelmann
pmc-11602816.description: The multi-grid reaction-diffusion master equation (mgRDME) provides a generalization of stochastic compartment-based reaction-diffusion modelling described by the standard reaction-diffusion master equation (RDME). By enabling different resolutions on lattices for biochemical species with different diffusion constants, the mgRDME approach improves both accuracy and efficiency of compartment-based reaction-diffusion simulations.

pmc-11605659.title: Comparison of localization and release of multivesicular bodies and secretory granules in islet cells: Dysregulation during type‐2 diabetes
pmc-11605659.creator: Priyadarshini Veerabhadraswamy, Kiran Lata, Sristi Dey, Prajakta Belekar, Lakshmi Kothegala, Vidya Mangala Prasad, Nikhil R. Gandasi
pmc-11605659.description: Multivesicular bodies (MVBs) are vesicles of endosomal origin containing intraluminal vesicles, which upon fusion with plasma membrane, secrete exosomes. They play a significant role in the physiology and pathology of type‐2 diabetes (T2D) due to disrupted intercellular communication. The role of MVBs and their influence on insulin secretory granules (ISGs) of β‐cells or their characterization is yet to be uncovered.

pmc-11619621.title: Improving the process of evaluating the quality of care in “maternal near miss” at hospital level: an action research study protocol
pmc-11619621.creator: Sedigheh Abdollahpour, Sanaz Mollazadeh, Shapour Badiee Avval, Talat Khadivzadeh
pmc-11619621.description: BackgroundThe fifth Millennium Development Goal aims to improve maternal health by reducing maternal mortality by 75% from 1990 to 2015. Consequently, utilizing quality care indicators and performance evaluations is crucial for providing effective services. This study aimed to evaluate the quality of care for critically ill mothers in hospitals through action research.

pmc-11673456.title: Hybrid Protocells Based on Coacervate‐Templated Fatty Acid Vesicles Combine Improved Membrane Stability with Functional Interior Protocytoplasm
pmc-11673456.creator: Jessica Lee, Fatma Pir Cakmak, Richard Booth, Christine D. Keating
pmc-11673456.description: Prebiotically‐plausible compartmentalization mechanisms include membrane vesicles formed by amphiphile self‐assembly and coacervate droplets formed by liquid–liquid phase separation. Both types of structures form spontaneously and can be related to cellular compartmentalization motifs in today's living cells. As prebiotic compartments, they have complementary capabilities, with coacervates offering excellent solute accumulation and membranes providing superior boundaries.

pmc-11707733.title: The Association of Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio and Other Complete Blood Count Parameters with Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events Risk Score in Patients with Non-ST Segment Elevation – Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Single-Center Study
pmc-11707733.creator: Ali Safaa Abduljabbar, Muataz Fawzi Hussein
pmc-11707733.description: BackgroundThe involvement of inflammation in the start and advancement of atherosclerotic plaques in acute coronary syndrome has been clarified. White blood cell count and its differential are key inflammatory markers in cardiovascular disease, with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) emerging as a marker of inflammation and a predictor of mortality in patients with acute coronary syndrome.

pmc-12375083.title: Thymoquinone mediated hedgehog pathway activation and gut microbiota modulation in mouse colitis
pmc-12375083.creator: Xixiang Huang, Tong Sun, Linxia Xu, Wei Liu, Zhi Ren, Zhenzeng Ma, Hailun Zheng, Dapeng Li, Qiangwu Wang, Xiquan Ke
pmc-12375083.description: To investigate the treatment of ulcerative colitis by thymoquinone (TQ) through the Hedgehog signaling pathway and the composition of intestinal microbiota. A total of 24 male Balb/C mice were randomly divided into blank group, model group, thymoquinone low-dose group (20 mg/kg) and thymoquinone high-dose group (80 mg/kg), with 6 mice in each group.

pmc-12468800.title: Automated Detection of Periodontal Bone Loss in Two-Dimensional (2D) Radiographs Using Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review
pmc-12468800.creator: Alin M. Iacob, Marta Castrillón Fernández, Laura Fernández Robledo, Enrique Barbeito Castro, Matías Ferrán Escobedo Martínez
pmc-12468800.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Artificial intelligence is an emerging tool that is being used in multiple fields, including dentistry. An example of this is the diagnosis of periodontal bone loss by analyzing two-dimensional (2D) radiographs (periapical, bitewing, and panoramic). Objectives: The objectives of this systematic review are to bring together the existing evidence and evaluate the effectiveness of the different artificial intelligence architectures that have been used in recent studies.

pmc-13028889.title: Purified Diets Lacking Fermentable Fiber Reduce Microbial Diversity, Alter Epithelial Transcriptome, and Exacerbate Colitis
pmc-13028889.creator: Emma Griffith Thomas, Beulah Favour Ortutu, Jacob Connor Watson, Ethan Ong, Kaitlyn Eileen Blankley, Angela Meaurio Martin, Smriti Shankar, Dongmei Zhang, Devon Joseph Boland, Chia-Shan Wu
pmc-13028889.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Dietary fibers play key roles in shaping gut microbiome and intestinal homeostasis. While purified diets offer experimental precision and reproducibility in rodent models, they omit the complex mixture of fermentable and non-fermentable fibers found in grain-based chow diets. We hypothesized that excluding fermentable fiber impairs intestinal homeostasis by reducing microbial metabolites and altering the colonic epithelial transcriptome, thereby increasing susceptibility to inflammation.

pmc-13312690.title: Gabapentin to achieve HIV viral load suppression in people with risky drinking in Mbarara, Uganda: study protocol for a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial (GRAIL)
pmc-13312690.creator: Ve Truong, Allen Kekibiina, Winnie R Muyindike, Natalia Gnatienko, Judith I Tsui, Nneka I Emenyonu, Debbie M Cheng, Judith A Hahn, Olivia Allison, Matthew J Bullard, Karsten Lunze, Jeffrey H Samet
pmc-13312690.description: BackgroundEnding the HIV epidemic requires achieving HIV viral load (HVL) suppression for key populations including those with risky drinking. Gabapentin can decrease alcohol use and thus holds potential for improving medication adherence and HIV viral load suppression for individuals with HIV and risky drinking.

pmc-13362914.title: A Review of Machine Learning Applications in Mechanical Metamaterial Design
pmc-13362914.creator: Galymzhan Turysbekov, Ulanbek Auyeskhan, Andrei Yankin, Asma Perveen, Didier Talamona
pmc-13362914.description: Highlights Integrating Machine Learning with metamaterial design enables the development of innovative structures with unprecedented properties, applying different ML architectures.Machine Learning techniques can significantly accelerate the design cycle, generating novel designs using inverse design frameworks.Emerging trends toward multifunctional materials and autonomous discovery systems show strong potential for addressing challenges related to interpretability and manufacturability.

pmc-13548497.title: “I Am Not Struggling Alone”: communicating support through peer mutual aid to reduce academic stress transmission and emotional contagion in large university classes
pmc-13548497.creator: Shi Yin, Ruqiao Wu, Wenqi Ma, Yifan Ou
pmc-13548497.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Large university classes are important communication environments in which students observe, interpret, and exchange stress-related information. Academic stress may therefore spread not only through individual experience but also through interpersonal communication and social interpretation,and shared meaning-making processes. How students communicate about academic challenges, interpret peers’ stress-related cues, and construct shared understandings of academic pressure may therefore influence whether stress becomes socially amplified or collectively managed.

pmc-13554801.title: DENND3-p.R534S disrupts dyadic microdomain architecture to drive potentially pro-arrhythmic calcium and electrophysiologic instability
pmc-13554801.creator: Shan Gao, Changsung John Kim, Dan Ye, David J Tester, John R Giudicessi, Michael J Ackerman
pmc-13554801.description: AimsInherited ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) frequently occur in the absence of pathogenic variants in canonical ion channel genes, suggesting alternative mechanisms of electrical instability. DENND3 is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor that regulates Rab GTPase-mediated trafficking, but its role in cardiac excitation-contraction coupling and membrane microdomain organization remains undefined.

pmc-13700374.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWe developed a novel, community pharmacy-based, pharmacist-driven atrial fibrillation (AF) stroke prevention model involving pharmacist prescription of oral anticoagulants (OAC) in Alberta, Canada. Generalizability to healthcare systems outside Canada is unknown.ObjectiveWe recruited 5 California pharmacies for a proof-of-concept pilot study aimed at evaluating the prevalence of “actionable” AF and the feasibility, safety, and barriers to implementing a pharmacist OAC prescription program.MethodsBefore implementation, pharmacist and physician stakeholders were surveyed to identify potential barriers.

uslaw-usc-t49-s24309.title: 49 U.S.C. § 24309 — Retaining and maintaining facilities
uslaw-usc-t49-s24309.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s24309.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Part C (Passenger Transportation); Chapter 243 (Amtrak). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions.— In this section— (1) “facility” means a rail line, right of way, fixed equipment, facility, or real property related to a rail line, right of way, fixed equipment, or facility, including a signal system, passenger station and repair tracks, a station building.
